Header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Nina Park (CSM), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions), Priya Patel (Novus CTO), Liam O'Connor (Novus ML Eng), Sara Gomez (Novus DevOps), Marcus Lee (Novus SRE)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync to review benchmark comparisons (Redwood vs baseline provider VendorX).
- Discussed latency percentiles, throughput/QPS, warm vs cold starts, KV/prefix caching, batching configs, and cost tradeoffs.
- Agreed on focused p95 test for 8k context and to share raw logs/spreadsheet.

Topics:

- Next steps and action items for final evaluation

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, jumping right in today we have benchmark results to walk through, Evan will run us through the numbers.
[00:12] Evan Brooks: cool thanks Maya, hi Priya, Liam, Sara quick reminder these are the weekly syncs, i pulled the runs from last night, there's a few runs flagged as warm and a couple cold starts so watch the p95 numbers not just the avg
[00:28] Priya Patel: thanks, and sorry if I joined a bit late, real quick, our target is 200 qps steady with peaks to 600 qps for certain workflows, and p95 latency target is sub 300ms if possible, p99 ideally under 600ms.
[00:44] Evan Brooks: got it, those are the targets we used to compare. so baseline provider (VendorX) in their managed env we measured p95 around 410 ms on 2k context, at 200 qps sustained, and p99 ~920 ms. Redwood Dedicated (config: 4xA100-like nodes, batching tuned) came in at p95 260 ms and p99 at 530 ms for same workload.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: quick question - those numbers with or without kv cache?
[01:08] Evan Brooks: those are with prefix/KV cache enabled, TTL 10m, cache hit rates about 38% on the test traces. without cache p95 jumped to 420 on Redwood.
[01:18] Sara Gomez: is that comparing same model quantization? baseline used 8-bit quant, we used 4-bit QAT?
[01:23] Evan Brooks: good call - baseline run we pulled was their standard 8-bit quant. our recommended production run used 4-bit quant + some operator fusion which lowered memory and allowed larger batch sizes, that helped throughput and reduced latency. there might be a mismatch there - we noted that in the notes.
[01:40] Marcus Lee: network variance - our infra team saw spikes when cold starting across the cloud region, could that be the reason for vendorX higher p99?
[01:46] Nina Park: yeah network/peering and VPC egress rules can add jitter - we saw about 30-80ms variance when peering wasn't optimally configured in the test harness.
[01:58] Evan Brooks: exactly - in our Redwood tests we ran both routed and colocated setups; colocated (same region + private peering) reduces tail by ~50-70ms on average.
[02:10] Priya Patel: ok so practical question - for our compliance needs we probably need private deployment, is Redwood going to match these numbers in Private mode too?
[02:18] Maya Chen: yes - Dedicated and Private use the same runtime, the difference is network/infra control - we can replicate the Dedicated config on-prem or in VPC but the peering/networking needs to be tuned. we'll document recommended firewall rules and MTU tweaks.
[02:32] Liam O'Connor: what's the cost delta vs VendorX for those numbers? vendorX pricing is kinda opaque.
[02:36] Maya Chen: fair - we'll send the pricing delta. ballpark, with our batching and quantization suggested we estimate 25-40% lower token cost vs baseline given similar accuracy (depends on model size and QPS). I'll attach the spreadsheet.
[02:52] Evan Brooks: also a note on batching: baseline used a static batch size of 8 which hurt latency at low QPS. we used dynamic batching with a max batch of 32 and target latency SLO 250ms, and it adapted well. at 200 qps average batch sizes were 6-10 which kept p95 down.
[03:10] Priya Patel: any AI safety/regression concerns when using 4-bit quant? we run clinical summarization so quality is critical.
[03:18] Evan Brooks: we ran our evaluation harness on 500 sample prompts - quality regressions were within tolerance (<1.5% BLEU-like metric delta, subjective pass-rate 96%). but you should run your domain prompts; that's part of the POC.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: can we see the raw traces? the timeline shows spikes around 00:05:32 in several runs.
[03:37] Nina Park: yes, we'll share the full trace logs and the aggregated sheet. look for the run labeled "2026-09-22-peak-run" in the spreadsheet. note transcripts sometimes reference that run as 22-sep but filenames vary.
[03:53] Sara Gomez: on the private deployment side we have KMS and HSM integrations to validate - do you have the SOC2 docs?
[03:58] Maya Chen: yep we'll include the SOC2 pack and KMS integration guide in the follow up.
[04:04] Jordan Li: a couple technical things from the SE side: we recommend enabling persistent KV cache with cold-warm prewarm on startup and setting cache TTLs to 5-15m depending on session churn. also set dynamic_batch_max to 32, dynamic_batch_timeout_ms 12. these improved our throughput in the tests.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: small nit - the test harness uses grpc vs http, any difference there?
[04:29] Evan Brooks: few ms differences, grpc tends to be slightly faster at scale. we tested both; telemetry included the protocol used in notes column.
[04:36] Priya Patel: can you repeat the p95 numbers for 8k context? our long context docs are critical.
[04:42] Evan Brooks: yes for 8k context baseline VendorX p95 was ~980 ms (very noisy), Redwood Dedicated with H100-like nodes and tuned kv/cache/dynamic batching hit p95 ~420 ms and p99 ~1.1s - note we have a couple of outlier runs where p99 jumped to 1.6s during cold-starts.
[05:05] Marcus Lee: 1.1s p99 for 8k is borderline for our UX flows, can you do focused 95th runs?
[05:10] Evan Brooks: yes that's in the action items, we'll run focused p95 tests and disable a few noisy variables to isolate network vs model perf.
[05:17] Maya Chen: to set expectations - for 8k contexts optimization helps but there's inherent compute cost, one levers is to use splitted prompt strategy (prefix compressing) and aggressive caching, another is model distillation or using a trimmed model for long context. both have tradeoffs.
[05:33] Priya Patel: sounds reasonable. one more - during the poc we saw a run where throughput dropped at 03:21 and we lost about 10% of requests returning 500s - any idea?
[05:42] Evan Brooks: i flagged that run - looks like autoscaler oscillation in the test harness interacting with small rolling restarts; we have a fix for the test infra and will re-run that scenario.
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: for the benchmarks please include the raw cli commands or k8s manifests you used so we can reproduce.
[05:58] Jordan Li: yup we'll include the runner commands, pod specs, and the perf tooling commands.
[06:03] Priya Patel: ok thanks. next steps and recap?
[06:07] Maya Chen: recap - evan to run focused p95 tests for 8k by end of week, we'll share full spreadsheet and raw logs, redwood to send SOC2/security pack and pricing delta, novus to confirm QPS schedule and validate vpc readiness. we'll target next sync same time next week.
[06:24] Priya Patel: great thanks everyone.
[06:27] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and action items. bye.
